response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS t, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS n FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT t, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT t, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share_above, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: "Executed orders" means distinct orders that have at least one matching execution, so an order with several executions counts once.

Share is a type's count divided by the sum of counts across all types (including the NULL-type group). The overall average share is the unweighted mean of the per-type shares, which equals 1 divided by the number of types.

alternatives.interpretation: Count execution rows (each execution counts as one) instead of distinct orders.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.ordertune AS t, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT t, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT t, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share_above, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM a WHERE share > avg_share
